meta.face: A Frank of about sixty with a fair, weathered complexion and a LONG face dominated by a LONG, BROAD, gently DROOPING nose with a big, soft, rounded tip — small, DEEP-SET, warm brown eyes under BUSHY brown-grey brows that ARCH UP toward the centre in an earnest, pleading look, a smooth forehead, lean cheeks, a small mouth, a short, slightly RECEDING chin under a SHORT, FULL, CURLY brown-grey beard; brown-grey hair round a small monk's tonsure; the gaze earnest and compassionate, down toward the child.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; Wikipedia's lead image is a Victorian statue at Grantham. The book tells his resignation of Sens, the saving of Ovon from the gibbet and of two children from drowning, and his death at Fontenelle; its engraving shows him lifting Ovon from the gallows. The card keeps a rescued child and leaves the gibbet off. The long face with the big drooping nose and the curly beard is our choice, to keep him from `ansgar`, the clean-shaven square-browed Frankish missionary of the north.
